speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your generalized nonpruritic rash in detail, including when it appeared and its specific characteristics, while also telling me more about your recent high fever and seizure.

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Cytomegalovirus (Cytomegalovirus) infection, presenting with sepsis-like illness, seizures, and rash. The clinical picture of a febrile seizure with a subsequent generalized non-pruritic rash in an infant with up-to-date immunizations is highly suggestive of a viral exanthem, with CMV being a leading consideration given the severity of the fever and seizure. I will now proceed to confirm this diagnosis by requesting specific test results and images. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, blood culture, CMV PCR (blood and urine), and liver function tests. REQUEST IMAGES: Rash close-up photographs and any available ultrasound of the brain if the seizure was not fully resolved.
